item: New to faith and returning (new_to_faith) — the 40-day journey
angle: The path already lands in the right place. Nothing here is a rebuild. Two things are actually broken: the reading unit is a whole chapter when the day's teaching is one verse, and the second week has nothing holding it. So: shrink the unit to what the day is about, put one plain sentence under the hard words, make coming back after a gap feel ordinary, clear the one card that has no business on this screen, and instrument it so the next decision is made on data instead of on a hunch. The photo plate, the sage, the paper reading panel and the Superdesign landing all stay exactly as they are.
thesis: A new believer is given one verse of teaching and served forty-two verses of chapter. Fix the unit, not the look: each day is the day's own verses, one short teaching, two questions, one tap done — and the whole chapter is always one tap away for the day they want it. Then hold week two with three cheap things the research names: plain-language help for hard words, a return-after-a-gap that says nothing about the gap, and one human invitation on day 10. Everything ships behind one deploy preview Ashley approves.
principles: One day is one thought and a few verses, never a chapter. Research P1: newcomer plans work as 'one thought plus a few verses'; cross-cutting #3: the felt need is a smaller unit of reading, not more content.

Nothing on this Home may compete with the sage journey button. Ashley, 1 Sep 2026: 'any text on the screen must be related to that button' (rulings packet, feedback_daily_word_today_rebuild_rejected line 20).

Never ask what the app already knows, and never count what would shame. The journey is day-numbered, not date-numbered, so a gap costs nothing by construction — say so, then move on. Cross-cutting #6: streaks work until they shame; repair, don't reset.

Hard words get one plain sentence, never a commentary. Research P1: 60% of Americans cannot name five Commandments; live config has commentary/greekHebrew/wordStudies all off for this path on purpose — a glossary is not a commentary.

Rich and warm, never stripped. Photo hero, sage, ivory canvas, the white paper reading panel in both themes, Georgia serif. Locked look (project_daily_word_platform_polish); the 1 Sep 'completely stripped' revert is the standing warning.
The returning reader is welcomed, not interviewed. Research P1: the returning line 'says come back, nothing to explain' — so it is one inclusive sentence, not a second door competing with Read.
Any change to the opening screen ships behind a preview link Ashley approves first. Ruling: owner-preview-gated, same class as the locked look.

journey.day0: Cold device. startGraceSeriesIfCold('default') writes dw_setup={new_to_faith,'default'} and enrolls the 40-day journey before React mounts (App.tsx:68, coldStart.ts:84-100) — credit-free, no cloud stamp. Day1Landing paints full-screen: wordmark, language switch, 'Day 1 of 40 · New & Returning to Faith', 'Grace Changes Everything', ONE new welcome line naming both the first-timer and the returner, one sage Read, and the quiet 'Not new to faith? Choose your path' link. Zero decisions, no gate, works fully offline (copy and the KJV verse are bundled).
journey.first_session: Read expands the reading in place: verse card, three pastoral beats, Day 1's two Reflect & Respond questions, 'Day 1 of 40', 'Mark as read'. New: up to two hard words in the pastoral text carry a dotted underline; tapping one opens a small sheet with one plain sentence. Mark as read stamps dw_reading_done (local date), advances the journey, records the streak, fires dw-reading-completed. Then, strictly sequenced and never stacked: PathAskedOnce ('Day 1, done.') → push ask → later the email nudge. All three unchanged.
journey.return_visit: Day 2 onward the tab shell renders. Home is: header cluster, greeting, the five-minute promise line (first three days), then the journey hero — photo plate, 'Day 2 of 40 · New & Returning to Faith', the day's title, the sage progress bar, one sage Read. The Sermon Notes row is gone from this path except in the Sunday window. Read opens the full-screen Day N surface: the day's own verses already open, the teaching, the two questions, Mark Complete.
journey.week2: This is where the path is lost today and where the work goes. The day's verses (not the chapter) keep the five-minute promise true. Word help keeps the teaching readable. On day 10, once, below Mark Complete: one invitation to have someone at Futures check in — an intake action, not a chat. Push, if they took it, names the journey and never the streak.
journey.missed_day: Nothing is lost and nothing is said about the gap. currentDay only advances on completion, so day 7 is still waiting. The single change: when the last completed day is two or more days ago, the greeting reads 'Welcome back, {first}. You left off on day 6.' and the hero shows day 7 as normal. No streak on this path, no red, no catch-up, no apology.
journey.seasonal: The journey already is the time-boxed 40-day challenge the research says drives spikes (cross-cutting #5). The only seasonal move worth building here is one optional line on the Day 1 landing when a church-wide start is running, read from a single new field in books/faith-pathway.json so it is a content edit, not a deploy. Low priority; not part of the first two weeks.

comfort_access: Two routes, and neither may sit on this path's Home. (1) Today: the PathSwatch in the Home header opens the one 'Where are you today?' sheet; 'I'm going through something hard' is one tap and, per the ruling, that tap saves and opens comfort. The journey is not lost — dw_pathway_progress is untouched, so switching back returns them to the exact day. That behaviour is already correct and should be stated in the sheet's own copy nowhere, because it already works. (2) When the cross-cutting one-tap comfort ships (research build #2: a persistent comfort tap that opens comfort WITHOUT rewriting the saved path), on this path it belongs in the Day N surface's action row beside Share — on the reading, where the person is when it hits them — and never on Home, where nothing may compete with the sage journey button (Ashley, 1 Sep). It must open comfort as a visit and must not write dw_setup. Crisis-language detection, the region-correct line and the human next step are that design's job, not this one's; this path only names where the door is.
reminders: The push ask already fires at the right moment and stays: after the first Mark as read, after PathAskedOnce, never stacked (ruled decision 1, evidence-timed via dw-reading-completed). Three changes downstream of it. (1) Copy: push-send.js sends a rotating chapter from a fixed 40-passage list, so a new believer on day 5 is pushed 'Psalms 119' — a chapter their journey has nothing to do with. Store the path on the subscription and send a journey-named message instead: title 'Your next day', body 'New & Returning to Faith — about five minutes.' No progress lookup is needed and none is possible, because the journey is day-numbered, not date-numbered. (2) Never the streak: no 'your streak is about to end' copy on this path, ever (cross-cutting #6 — guilt-framed streak reminders drive opt-out and uninstall). (3) Spanish and Portuguese templates do not exist: TEMPLATES has en and id only, so an es/pt reader of a fully translated 40-day journey gets English pushes. Claude drafts es/pt, Ashley approves before ship (translated-content ruling). Cadence stays as it is — one a day, at the hour they set in Settings, hourly cron with the two-hour catch-up window. Behaviour-inferred send time (research P2) is a later change and needs the instrumentation below first. Verification note: pushSupported() allowlists only futuresdailyword.com/www/localhost, so none of this is testable on the deploy preview — prod or localhost only.
instrumentation: FIRST, THE BLOCKER: track() only writes to Supabase when dw_profile.email exists (src/utils/analytics.ts:75-77). A new believer has no email until well after day 1, so the entire funnel this design is about is invisible in the dashboard today. GA4 still receives it; Supabase does not. Fix with an anonymous dw_device_id accepted by track-activity, or read D1/D7/D30 from GA4. Nothing else on this list is trustworthy until this is done.
journey_day_open — detail: day number. Proves the hero tap and gives session-by-day.
journey_day_complete — detail: day number. The completion curve by day; this is the day-2 and day-7 number no public source will ever supply (research cross-cutting #7).
journey_chapter_expanded vs journey_verses_only — proves or kills the reading-unit change. If nobody expands, the chapter was never the point; if most do, revert it.
word_help_open — detail: the term. The glossary tap rate the research names as the test for literacy scaffolding.
journey_gap_return — detail: days since last completion. Proves the no-shame return and sizes the missed-day population.
journey_invite_sent and journey_invite_dismissed — day 10 relational move, accept rate.
push_opt_out — named in research build #1 as the reminder health metric; not tracked today.
day1_abandon — Read tapped, Mark as read never reached in the session. The single number that says whether the landing works.

Add all of these to TRACKED_EVENTS in src/utils/analytics.ts:31 — the allowlist silently drops anything not in it, so a new event name with no allowlist entry looks like zero usage rather than an error.
Rollup: one nightly job producing D1/D7/D30 and completion-by-day, split by path. Report new_to_faith separately from the other four or the journey's curve disappears into the congregation's.

LIVE TODAY — LanguageSwitch on both the Day 1 landing and Home: changes language live, no reload, and the whole 40-day journey plus its questions exist in es/pt/id.

LIVE TODAY — books/faith-pathway.json (and _es/_pt/_id) is network-first with cache as offline fallback only, fixed in PR #84. Anyone who can edit that file changes a lesson, a title, a theme or the two questions and returning readers get it on their second open. No code change, no sw.js edit, no cache bump. This is the real content lever on this path and it should be documented as such.

NEW, SAME MECHANISM — books/glossary.json plus _es/_pt/_id. Terms and their one-sentence definitions are edited as content, live on the second open, no deploy of sw.js. Put it under /books precisely so it inherits the network-first rule.

NEW, SMALL BUILD — move the push templates out of push-send.js into a table keyed by lang and path, so reminder wording is edited without a function deploy. Today every word of every push is hardcoded in netlify/functions/push-send.js.

NOT SELF-SERVE, AND NAME IT AS SUCH — the day-10 invitation's recipient. Campuses come from CAMPUSES in src/data/tokens.ts and there is no admin for who receives a request. Who at each campus gets it is an owner decision, and adding a campus is a developer edit.

STILL A DEVELOPER EDIT — sectionOrder per persona (persona-config.ts), the Day 1 landing copy (src/data/day1-landing.ts, generated questions block pinned by a test), the gating logic for when the landing and the asked-once screen fire (coldStart.ts, App.tsx), REAL_CHOICE_SOURCES (coldStart.ts:21), and the two out-of-sync milestone lists (streak.ts:14 and GreetingSection.tsx:6).

open_decisions: Approve the deploy preview before anything merges. Everything here lands on one branch and one preview link; the Day 1 landing and the Day N reading are both owner-preview-gated and the 1 Sep revert is the reason. Verify translations on prod, not the preview — a DW deploy preview gets 403 from its own /api and silently falls back to offline KJV.

The glossary term list and its wording in four languages. Claude drafts, Ashley approves before ship (translated-content ruling). Proposed starting set for days 1–14: grace, saved, righteousness, repentance, condemnation, faith, Holy Spirit, baptism, sin, gospel.

Whether to reorder the 40 days toward narrative-first. The research argues for it; the data model argues against it, because currentDay is an index and reordering rewrites what day 7 means for everyone already on day 7. If yes, it needs a migration plan, not just a JSON edit.
Who at each campus receives the day-10 check-in request, and what they are expected to do with it. No recipient exists today.

Whether the day-10 invitation may require an email address (it routes through the existing prayer intake, which does). If he will not gate it behind an email, the card should be dropped rather than softened.
What Home shows a reader who has finished all 40 days. The Day N surface has a final-day line; the journey hero does not, and would sit on '✓ Read today' for day 40 indefinitely.
risks: Verse-range rendering depends on [N] markers in the returned text. If a translation or the offline KJV returns text without markers, a naive filter renders an empty panel. Mandatory fallback: unresolvable range → render the whole chapter, silently. The known CLAUDE.md gotcha that fetchKJV dumps raw JSON for object-shaped chapters makes this a real path, not a theoretical one.

Ashley has already seen and approved the whole-chapter Day N surface (PR #81 shipped on his 'merge and deploy' with '42 tappable ESV verses' in the record). Shrinking the reading may read to him as taking something away. Frame it in the preview as 'the chapter is one tap under the verses' and show day 3 specifically — one verse taught, 42 served.

Removing the Sermon Notes row from this path outside the Sunday window removes a route for a QR guest who arrives on a Monday. That is what the ruling says to do, and the row still returns in the Sunday window, but it is a deliberate loss worth naming out loud.

Dotted underlines are new visual texture on a page whose look is locked. Cap at two per day, lesson text only, no colour change, no icon. If it reads busy in the preview, drop the underline and keep the sheet reachable from a long-press instead.
The day-10 invitation is the one place in this path that requires an email. At day 10 that is defensible; if it lands as a wall it will read as the gate Ashley removed in August.

Any new overlay on the Day 1 landing inherits an existing hazard: Day1Landing itself uses useModalA11y(true) plus role=dialog aria-modal, and already hosts ChoosePathSheet on the grounds that the sheet's trap is document-level. The word-help sheet on that screen must be checked against the same trap before it ships, or Escape and the back gesture will close the landing underneath it.

Any edit to books/faith-pathway.json or the new glossary.json is invisible to returning users until their second open after deploy. Do not judge either from a prod bundle grep — check the service-worker strategy for the asset class first.
